story: The lighthouse keeper kept a tin box of words that visitors left behind. Most were ordinary: harbour, kettle, rain. On the first cold morning of the year she found a new card wedged under the door, and on it, in careful green ink, was the word "snollygoster". She did not know what it meant. She said it aloud to the gulls, who were unimpressed, and then to the lamp, which was patient with her as always. By noon she had decided it must describe the particular silver of the sea before a storm. By evening she was sure it was the name of a small, stubborn fish. That night she wrote both guesses on the back of the card and filed it with the others. Somewhere, she hoped, a stranger was waiting to tell her she was wrong. Until then, "snollygoster" belonged to her, and she said it every time the light came round.
